top_choice_rationale: P001 (Melitz and Helpman, firm heterogeneity and selection) is the contribution that most changed what trade economists measure and how policy is evaluated. Its selection and reallocation mechanisms have been tested against firm-level data in many countries for over two decades, and it spread into industrial organisation and quantitative macro. The credit gap for Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum is a real risk. I judge it manageable with a citation worded around the mechanism and a Scientific Background that describes the empirical precursors. P002 (Grossman and Helpman) is a close second. It has cleaner two-person attribution and no maturity concern, but its protection-for-sale predictions are less consistently confirmed, so its influence runs ahead of its confirmation. I would not credit Helpman in both strands. P004 (Autor, Hanson, Dorn) has credible design-based evidence, but magnitudes, shift-share identification and task-strand attribution remain contested. P003 has a broad programme, but weaker identification, unclear apportionment across the three names and adjacency to the 2024 prize place it below. I rank an award above no award.
recusal_note: No candidate-specific connection is apparent from the profile. My research on pricing, exchange-rate pass-through and international trade is thematically close to P001 and P002. I co-authored a 2026 paper with the chair, John Hassler, and former chair Tore Ellingsen, neither of whom is a candidate. My spouse's public political role is noted as a public fact only, with no apparent bearing on any candidate. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
